notes: **Presenter:** Joshua. One person, one list, in video order.

**Before recording anything:** Joshua has a Qube login in Chrome on his own laptop. Nothing in this video uses Claude, Codex or the terminal: everything is typed into Qube itself. Don't show any API keys, emails, account names or numbers.
**Recording order for the Qube clips** (one run, they build on each other): A2 → A5 → A6 → A8. Record A2 in one go, then cut it into the parts below.
**The example stock is Tencent (0700.HK).** It's only an example input, never a call: no "buy" on screen next to it outside the typed sentence, and "Example strategy" on every frame that shows it.

open.text: **Hong Kong in the hook.** The hook says "A trading company just released…" because nothing in the skills says where TQX is based. If TQX is a Hong Kong company, say so and the hook gets the original's place back: "A Hong Kong company just released an entire AI hedge fund, and it runs on your laptop for free."

**Example stock.** Tencent (0700.HK) is set as the example input (A2), so the run is on a Hong Kong stock and differs from J023's NVDA. Say if you'd rather use another; it's only typed, never called a buy.

rows.how: 1. Phone vertical (9:16), eye level, office lights on, lock focus and exposure. 2. Move the phone in close (face fills the frame) and record, three times each: "And the part nobody's talking about?" · "Comment QUBE and I'll send you the link for the free sign-up."

1. Pexels, search exactly: `stock ticker numbers screen`. 2. Pick a clip of glowing white, green and red price numbers on a dark screen, no logos, no brand or exchange names, no faces. 3. Not honeycove's clip. 4. Trim to 1.5s (1.0s is used).

rows.file: J027_A2_run.mp4 · 1920×1080 · up to 90s (sped up and cut in the edit) · plus J027_A2_typed.png, _code.png, _dates.png, _run.png, _result.png, _trades.png
rows.how: 1. Chrome on his laptop, full screen, zoom 125%, no tabs or bookmarks showing, logged in to Qube. Close anything that shows his email or account name. 2. Start a screen recording of the whole screen (QuickTime → File → New Screen Recording). 3. Start a new strategy by describing it in plain English. 4. Type exactly, by hand, don't paste: `Buy Tencent (0700.HK) when it closes above its 20-day high. Sell once it's up 10% from where I bought, or if it falls 5% from where I bought. Put $2,000 in each trade. Start with $10,000.` 5. Take a screenshot of the typed sentence before sending it (typed.png). 6. Send it. Keep recording until Qube has written the code. Hold 3s. Screenshot (code.png). 7. Set the backtest to the last five years. Screenshot the date setting with the start and end dates showing (dates.png). 8. Run the backtest. Screenshot while it's running (run.png). Keep recording until the result appears, with the price chart and its trades marked. Hold 3s. Screenshot (result.png). 9. Open the list of every trade. Scroll top to bottom in about 3s, then scroll back to a spot where at least 3 losing trades are on screen together. Hold 3s. Screenshot (trades.png). **CHECK: the dates must cover five years or less (Qube tests on up to five years of real price data). If Qube runs longer, tell Mark before the edit.** **CHECK: the trade list must have real losing trades. If no trade lost money, stop and send Mark the screenshot; line 6 needs a real losing trade, never a staged one.** **CHECK: if Qube can't run Tencent (0700.HK), stop and tell Mark before picking another stock. Don't change any number Qube shows.**
rows.what: The Qube run: typing the strategy, the code, the backtest, the result, every trade

rows.how: 1. On the A2 strategy, open Qube's AI optimization. 2. Start a screen recording. 3. Let the AI suggest changes and test them. Record until it shows at least one tested change and the list of versions. Hold 2s on the versions. 4. Screenshot the first suggested change, with its wording readable (suggestion.png). Then screenshot the list of versions, with the newest tested version on screen (versions.png). **CHECK: the suggestion must be Qube's own words. Don't retype or edit it.** **CHECK: the version list must show at least one version Qube tested after its suggestion. Don't change any number on it.**

1. Put trades.png (from A2) on the A3 card. 2. Pick the losing trade with the biggest loss on screen. 3. notes: **Recreating:** @ai.honeycove · https://www.instagram.com/p/Dao8zl4Of3I/ · copy its rhythm: a visual change about every 2s (18 cuts in 37.8s); split screen (B-roll top half, presenter bottom half) between full-screen screenshot cards; every screenshot a rounded card on one solid colour with the key phrase swiped in yellow highlighter; Joshua full frame on "the part nobody's talking about", then a zoom into one losing trade boxed in yellow; the last line stops dead into the CTA.

**Layout:** two layouts only. **Split:** top half 1080×960 (B-roll or Qube screen, scaled to fill, centred), Joshua in the bottom half 1080×960. **Card:** full screen 1080×1920, solid gold #E8B04B background (A3), the screenshot as a rounded card 960px wide, centred. Captions 2–4 words, house preset "TQX Captions", sitting on the split line (y = 960) when split and at y = 1380 on cards. Our own look (gold background, highlighter #FFE14D), not honeycove's green asterisk background or caption box.

**Highlighter:** a #FFE14D rectangle at 70% opacity, multiply blend, 6px taller than the text, wiping left to right in 0.3s on the spoken word named in the row. One highlight per card unless the row says two.
**Times** are estimates at Joshua's pace (3.2 words a second, about 42s). Re-time to the real take.

lines.text: A Hong Kong university just open sourced an entire AI hedge fund and it runs on your laptop for free.
It's called Vibe Trading and this is insane.
You type what you want in plain English and a whole team of AI agents goes to work.
One researches, one builds the strategy, one runs the backtest, another reviews the risk.
A real trading desk in your terminal.
It pulls live data from 18 sources across stocks, crypto and forex, and stress tests every strategy with Monte Carlo before you risk a single dollar.
And the part nobody's talking about, upload your real broker history and it tells you exactly which of your own habits are bleeding you money.
More than 400 pre-built quant strategies, 15,000 developers already on it.
